titre: The Terracotta Army of Xi'an, Discovered by Farmers (1974)
accroche: In March 1974, farmers digging a well near Xi'an come upon a clay army buried for more than 2,000 years.
contenu_vulgarise:
On March 29, 1974, in Lintong County, near Xi'an, Yang Zhifa, his five brothers, and their neighbor Wang Puzhi dig a well about 1.5 kilometers east of Qin Shi Huang's burial mound, at the foot of Mount Li, in a region threaded with underground springs. What they reach is an underground chamber holding an army of terracotta soldiers. In the years that follow, archaeologists uncover an army buried around 210 BCE to guard the tomb of China's first emperor: according to 2007 estimates, more than 8,000 soldiers, 130 chariots drawn by 520 horses, and 150 cavalry horses, spread over three pits, with a fourth left empty.

## Standardized Production, Two Thousand Years Before the Assembly Line

What is most striking is not the number but the method. The figures are made in workshops by government laborers and local craftsmen, using local clay. Heads, arms, legs, and torsos are shaped separately, fired, then assembled. The faces are made in molds (at least ten molds may have been used, according to Wikipedia), then clay is added after assembly to give each figure its own features. The result creates the illusion of thousands of unique individuals, when production in fact rests on interchangeable parts. Wikipedia classes the process as assembly-line production, and notes that some sculptors signed their names under the armpits of certain figures.

## What the Public Has Never Seen

The soldiers visitors see today are a uniform gray, and that is an optical illusion of history: originally they were painted with mineral pigments, cinnabar red, malachite green, azurite blue, charcoal black, under a layer of lacquer. In Xi'an's dry air, that lacquer can curl within fifteen seconds of exposure and flake off in four minutes; much of the color was lost in the minutes after the figures were uncovered. In other words, much of what the excavators saw in color disappeared almost at once.

Color is not the only fragility. The emperor's central tomb has still not been opened, perhaps, according to Wikipedia, out of concern for preserving what it contains. Britannica confirms that the tomb itself remains to be excavated: the army, for its part, came out of the ground by chance, under the shovels of farmers looking for water.

repere.texte: In Xi'an's dry air, the lacquer covering the soldiers' original paint can curl within fifteen seconds of exposure and flake off in four minutes: the original cinnabar red, malachite green, and azurite blue have largely disappeared shortly after the figures were uncovered.

carte.punch: More than 8,000 soldiers that all seem unique, assembled from standardized parts.
carte.idee: In 1974, farmers digging a well near Xi'an discover Emperor Qin's terracotta army: more than 8,000 soldiers, made of standardized parts and then individualized. Originally painted, they lost most of their color within minutes in the open air.

quiz.question: How did Emperor Qin's workshops produce 8,000 soldiers that are all different?
choix: By sculpting each soldier by hand, with no interchangeable parts
By assembling standardized parts, then sculpting a distinct face for each one
By casting all the soldiers in a single mold, reused 8,000 times
By hiring 8,000 sculptors, one per soldier, with no common step
quiz.explication: The workshops shaped heads, arms, legs, and torsos separately before assembly, the faces came from molds, and clay added after assembly individualized each figure: standardized bodies with faces that are all different, not an individual sculpture or a single mold.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Who discovered the Terracotta Army of Xi'an, and under what circumstances?
choix: Archaeologists carrying out a planned excavation in the Xi'an region
Railroad workers laying track near Lintong
Chinese soldiers on military maneuvers in Lintong County
Farmers digging a well near the emperor's burial mound
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Yang Zhifa, his five brothers, and their neighbor Wang Puzhi were digging a well on March 29, 1974 when they reached the underground chamber, which led to the discovery of the army.

quiz_supplementaire.question: Why have the soldiers' original colors almost all disappeared?
choix: Because archaeologists sandblasted them clean before display
Because the original clay held no pigment
Because the lacquer that fixed the colors curls and flakes off within minutes in the open air
Because the farmers repainted the statues before alerting the authorities
quiz_supplementaire.explication: The lacquer covering the paint can curl within fifteen seconds in Xi'an's dry air and flake off in four minutes, taking much of the color with it.
